Owner findings triaged per Law 3: obvious-harm misconfig / malicious-owner = INVALID; non-obvious footgun unknowingly enabling an exploit or breaking a story = VALID operational hazard. Law 1 governs disposition: nothing ruled invalid or questioned is deleted — every ruling is recorded here, a visible channel.

gitProvenanceEvidence.why: The sharpest INVALID challenge to M-01 is not the one the brief raised (the docblock) but one it did not: INTENTIONAL DESIGN. The project's own suite contains three tests literally named test_hook_revert_propagates_on_{stake,withdraw,claim} (test/PhlimboV3Test.t.sol:487/501/517) that attach a reverting hook and assert the revert. On its face that is a sponsor who knew, tested, and affirmed the behaviour — the textbook 'intentional design flagged as bug' false positive. It had to be answered with provenance, not argument.
findings: IPhlimboHook.sol was last touched by ac42de6 '[story-020] PhlimboV2 with fixed depletion, migrator role, and hook system' — the V2 hook-system commit. It has NEVER been modified since. It is a V2 artifact by commit provenance, not merely by its text.

test_hook_revert_propagates_on_withdraw was introduced by 8099db7 '[story-022] Phase 1a: verbatim V2 copy as PhlimboV3 + IPhlimboV3, V2 suite ported and green'. The test asserting the propagation is a VERBATIM V2 PORT, written for a contract that had pauseWithdraw.

story-030 (e32588d — the run-10 baseline) removed pauseWithdraw from PhlimboV3. Its --name-only diff touches .gas-snapshot, src/PhlimboV3.sol, src/interfaces/IPhlimboV3.sol, test/PhlimboV3Test.t.sol. It touched NO hook file: not IPhlimboHook.sol, not the hook tests. It deleted 163 lines of tests without revisiting a single hook artifact.

PhlimboV2.sol:280 NatSpec confirms the V2 escape hatch was deliberately hook-exempt: 'Emergency exit mechanism — strictly msg.sender-only. NOT delegatable to migrator. Does NOT claim rewards or update pool. Does NOT invoke any hook.'
gitProvenanceEvidence.conclusion: EVERY artifact evidencing 'intended design' — the docblock AND all three propagation tests — predates story-030 and was authored for a contract where the consequence was survivable. What story-020 intended and tested is 'a reverting hook reverts the outer call, atomically' (an ATOMICITY property; the withdraw test's own assertion message is 'state preserved on revert'). No test, docblock, or story anywhere asks 'and now how does the staker get their principal out?' — because until story-030 the answer was pauseWithdraw. The intent evidence is uniformly STALE: the sponsor never affirmed the freeze-with-no-exit consequence in the post-story-030 world. The 'intentional design' challenge therefore FAILS, and it fails on record rather than on rhetoric.
gitProvenanceEvidence.lawNote: Even had the intent been current, CLAUDE.md Law 2 forecloses the defence: 'Law 1 overrides: if a story's own intended behaviour would introduce an exploit, flag the unsafe story — do not bless a faithful-but-exploitable implementation.' Intentional-design is a C4 defence; this repo's hierarchy overrides C4 where they conflict. Recorded so the point is not re-litigated: in phlimbo-ea, 'it's intended' is never by itself a validity answer.

THE DECISIVE CHECK. Law-3 triage resolves to NON-OBVIOUS FOOTGUN -> VALID. Reasoning below in adminTriage.

adminTriage.question: The trigger is setHook(<non-zero>), onlyOwner, and hook == address(0) at the shipped config. Obvious misconfig (INVALID) or non-obvious footgun (VALID)? Test: would a competent, non-malicious owner be SURPRISED by this consequence?
adminTriage.verdict: SURPRISED = YES on the consequence -> FOOTGUN -> VALID (in scope as an operational hazard).
adminTriage.theOwnersActionIsNotTheHarm: This is the structural reason the reckless-admin pattern does not fit, and it is worth stating precisely because it is what separates this from the archetype. The invalid archetype ('admin sets price=0', 'admin points the oracle at a malicious token') has harm that is IMMEDIATE and DETERMINISTIC from the action — the owner could see it at the moment they act. Here the owner's action causes ZERO harm: the hook works, and the PoC's smoke test PASSES at setHook time (test F: bob, who stakes post-attach, exits fine). The harm requires a SUBSEQUENT THIRD-PARTY EVENT — a dependency registry pausing 30 days later, operated by someone who is not the Phlimbo owner. At the moment of freeze there is NO owner action. An owner cannot validate against a hazard that is absent when they act and arrives when they are not acting. That is the C4 Medium 'external requirements' shape, not the reckless-admin shape.
adminTriage.obviousnessOfMechanismVsConsequence: The strongest INVALID argument, stated at full strength and NOT strawmanned: IPhlimboHook.sol says 'a reverting hook will revert the outer call.' withdraw() is an outer call. Reverting hook -> withdraw reverts -> principal stuck. That is ONE short inferential step and it is not subtle. If that inference is the finding, the finding is obvious and invalid. Answer: it is not the finding. On PhlimboV2 — the ONLY contract that docblock names, three times — that exact inference TERMINATED at 'stuck, but pauseWithdraw is hook-exempt so the user still exits' (verified at PhlimboV2.sol:280). The mechanism was true and the catastrophic consequence was FALSE. story-030 deleted the terminator from V3 and updated neither the docblock nor the tests. The sentence's truth value never changed; its meaning did. An owner is entitled to read a documented behaviour in the safety context the document was written for — and here that entitlement is not a courtesy, it is provable from the commit graph: the doc is a story-020 V2 artifact, untouched since.
adminTriage.malicePreconditionOfTheDisclosure: The disclosure's own sentence binds the propagation to the MALICE frame: 'The owner of PhlimboV2 is trusted to set non-malicious hooks; a reverting hook will revert the outer call.' The malicious-hook case is Law-3 trusted and is expressly NOT reported (correctly — a malicious-owner vector would itself be invalid here). The reported case is a benign, correctly-written hook that begins reverting later for a reason it does not control. The disclosure and the finding barely overlap on the operative scenario.
adminTriage.absentAtThePointOfAction: setHook's NatSpec IN FULL (src/PhlimboV3.sol:331-333, read in source, not paraphrased): '@notice Sets the hook contract invoked after stake/withdraw/claim. @dev Accepts address(0) to disable the hook.' There is NO warning at the one load-bearing action in this finding. src/PhlimboV3.sol contains no hook-revert disclosure anywhere.
adminTriage.noPrivilegeEscalation: Confirmed and recorded against the opposite error: this is NOT a privilege-escalation finding and must not be dressed as one. No unprivileged path arms it (test_CODE001_G asserts setHook is onlyOwner and hook is zero-initialized). Its validity rests on the footgun limb of Law 3, not the escalation limb.

validityChecks.notes: VALID. Survives every known-invalid pattern, including two challenges beyond the brief's list (intentional-design; the mechanism-obviousness reading of the disclosure). The finding's validity does not depend on the propagation being undocumented — the submission concedes in §69 that it is documented, quotes the sentence verbatim, and calls a hidden-trap framing 'dishonest'. It depends on the CONSEQUENCE (pool-wide principal freeze, zero user recourse) having been created by story-030 and never disclosed, tested, or reconciled anywhere. That is a footgun.

checks.note: CHALLENGED AND CLEARED, and the challenge was checked rather than reasoned about. The finding references FlaxToken (lib/immutable/flax-token-v2 — a nested dep, OOS by the lib/** denylist), so the parent/fork rule had to be tested. It does not bite: FlaxToken is the TRIGGER's location, not the ROOT CAUSE's. The root cause is entirely first-party — PhlimboV3._claimRewards:913-918 credits unclaimablePhUSDOf[beneficiary] while PhlimboV3 exposes only claimUnclaimablePhUSD() (:644), a msg.sender-only pull with no on-behalf variant, and MigratorV2V3 has no call-through to it. VERIFIED BY EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION (not a truncated grep): MigratorV2V3's complete external/public surface is seedUsers:144, migrate:172, migrateOne:235, skipCurrent:284, claimUnclaimable:302, withdrawAll:318, userCount:370. The near-miss is claimUnclaimable(address token):302 — its NAME suggests it closes the gap; reading its BODY shows it reads the migrator's OWN unclaimable[token][msg.sender] mapping and does IERC20(token).safeTransfer from the migrator's OWN balance. It never calls phlimboV3.claimUnclaimablePhUSD(). withdrawAll:318 likewise sweeps balanceOf and cannot see un-minted phUSD. The ABI gap is real. Fixing FlaxToken would not fix this; fixing PhlimboV3 or MigratorV2V3 would.

CHALLENGED AND CLEARED. 'Is it speculative given the shipped config makes the leg dead code (desiredAPYBps == 0)?' — No, for the same reason as M-01 and the reasoning must stay consistent across the two. desiredAPYBps (:60) is a plain uint256 with no constructor initializer => 0 at deploy, and the leg is gated by `if (pendingPhUSDAmount > 0)` (:903) — verified in source. But the BANK CODE IS SHIPPED (story-031, this run's diff), the root cause is demonstrated in it, and the strand is proven by a positive-control PoC (test_ECON001_positiveControl_callThroughRecovers). Dormant CONFIG is not future CODE. desiredAPYBps is settable at :271-272 by routine product decision, at which point this arms with no code change whatsoever. Correctly handled as a SEVERITY GATE with explicit escalation triggers, never as a suppression (Law 1).

Law-3 triage -> NON-OBVIOUS FOOTGUN -> VALID. The trigger is an INDIVIDUAL setMinter(phlimbo,false) on a SHARED ecosystem token — a kill-switch an operator pulls to contain an unrelated minter incident elsewhere in Phoenix, with no visibility into PhlimboV3's migration state. Would a competent, non-malicious operator be SURPRISED that a containment action on FlaxToken permanently destroys migrating users' reward entitlements with no on-chain recovery? YES — decisively, because the contract's own docblock at :637-643 promises the opposite ('A pull that fails because authority is still missing SHOULD revert, leaving the bank intact (exactly the claimUnclaimableStable recoverability semantics)'), and that promise is FALSE for a beneficiary with no pull. A protocol whose documentation asserts a recoverability property it does not universally have cannot then call the owner reckless for relying on it. Not malice; not an obvious-harm misconfig. In scope. This mirrors run-10's DEDUP-10-001 triage, which reached VALID on the same kill-switch reasoning — consistency is deliberate.
checks.inversionWorthKeeping: The safe-config guidance inverts the usual intuition and that inversion is the finding's most useful operational output: the GLOBAL revokeAllMintPrivileges is SAFER here than the narrower individual setMinter(phlimbo,false), because a global revoke also breaks PhlimboV2's bare inline mint (PhlimboV2.sol:495), reverting migrateOne, which migrate catches as UserMigrationSkipped — leaving the user untouched and unharmed. The narrower action strands silently. An operator would never guess this; it belongs in the runbook verbatim.

validityChecks.notes: VALID as a Low footgun. Both challenges the brief raised were tested against source and neither bites. The severity dissent (1 Medium vs 3 Low) is NOT this stage's call and is not re-opened here — severity-classifier adjudicated it on the merits, adopted the dissent's MECHANISM (story-031 converted a loud, self-healing failure into a silent, permanent one) into fixGuidance.dissentDerivedRequirement, and rejected only its severity conclusion. That adjudication is sound and its disposition is Law-1 correct: the dissent's contribution survives the severity vote rather than dying with it.
validityChecks.recommendation: RETAIN as L-01. Do not suppress. Carry escalation TRIGGER 2 prominently — 'Is PhlimboV3's owner the same party as FlaxToken's owner?' is a deploy-config question a human answers in minutes, is unanswerable from the repo, and flips this to Medium if the answer is NO. It is the cheapest high-value open question in the run and this stage endorses escalating it.

validityChecks.label: L-02

checks.note: Root cause demonstrated in source and by PoC (test_ECON002_bankMintsFreshSupplyAfterEmergencyTransfer — PASS). Same desiredAPYBps==0 dormancy gate as L-01, handled as a severity gate not a suppression.

THE CHECK THIS FINDING HAD TO SURVIVE. The brief correctly required verification rather than accepting the finding's self-assessment, since pe7m2 was closed INVALID for proposing accounting inside the ejector seat. VERIFIED COMPLIANT — it has NOT drifted.

Law-3 -> non-obvious footgun. The ejector seat is BALANCE-based and visibly neutralizes the stable and promo banks (their tokens are swept, so their pulls revert), which invites the reasonable inference that it neutralizes all three. The phUSD bank's survival is invisible precisely BECAUSE it is un-minted — there is nothing in the balance for the owner to see. An owner concluding 'I have wound the protocol down and extinguished its obligations' after firing a terminal hatch would be genuinely surprised to learn a permissionless, un-pause-gated claim on FRESH supply outlived it. Not malice, not obvious harm.

ejectorSeatVerification.howChecked: Read the fix guidance in BOTH deduplicated-findings.json (DEDUP-11-003.fixGuidance) and classified-findings.json (CLASS-11-003.safeConfigGuidance) in full, then re-derived the mechanism from source rather than trusting either.
ejectorSeatVerification.recommendationAsWritten: 'OPERATIONAL, not structural. Add to the emergencyTransfer runbook a mandatory follow-up step: revoke PhlimboV3's phUSD minter role (FlaxToken.setMinter(phlimbo, false), or revokeAllMintPrivileges()) so the terminal action actually terminates the mint obligation. Document in SolvencyDetermination.md that emergencyTransfer alone does NOT extinguish the phUSD bank, unlike the stable/promo banks.'
ejectorSeatVerification.verdict: COMPLIANT. This is a RUNBOOK STEP executed OUTSIDE the hatch, on a DIFFERENT contract (FlaxToken), plus a documentation change. Zero accounting is proposed inside emergencyTransfer. The hatch's terminal, no-accounting design is respected AS-IS and the finding says so explicitly and unprompted: 'If a code change is ever preferred over the runbook step, the correct site is a documented note at :644 — NOT accounting in the hatch.' It fences itself off from pe7m2's error by name.
ejectorSeatVerification.structuralDistinction: The hazard LIVES OUTSIDE THE HATCH and this is what makes it categorically different from pe7m2. pe7m2 asked the ejector seat to do bookkeeping on its way out. This finding accepts that the ejector seat does no bookkeeping and observes that a SEPARATE function — claimUnclaimablePhUSD (:644) — outlives it. The defect is not in emergencyTransfer's design; it is that a permissionless mint-backed liability survives a terminal action that the operator believes is terminal.
sourceReVerified: emergencyTransfer (:360-378) is exactly a balanceOf sweep of phUSD/rewardToken/promoToken followed by _pause(). No accounting. Confirmed by reading the full function body.

claimUnclaimablePhUSD (:644) signature IN FULL: `function claimUnclaimablePhUSD() external nonReentrant {` — NO whenNotPaused modifier, so the hatch's _pause() does not gate it. It calls phUSD.mint(msg.sender, amount) — it MINTS, it does not transfer, so the sweep provably cannot reach it (there is no balance to sweep). Both halves of the finding's mechanism confirmed independently.

The omission of whenNotPaused is DELIBERATE and correct on its own terms — the docblock at :633-636 explains beginFlush pauses the contract, so a gate would lock users out of self-rescue for the whole flush window. The finding does not ask for that gate, which is another point of pe7m2 non-overlap: it does not attack a deliberate design decision, it identifies an interaction that decision has with a terminal action.
ejectorSeatVerification.doNotCloseAsPe7m2: RECORDED AS A STANDING FLAG: this finding must NOT be closed as a pe7m2 re-file. It is the nearest neighbour to a closed-INVALID entry in this project and the closure would be superficially plausible to a future triager who reads only the function names 'emergencyTransfer' + 'unclaimable'. It is verified NOT one, twice, by two agents independently.

validityChecks.notes: VALID as a Low footgun, and the ejector-seat principle is respected in both letter and spirit. Discharges an explicit Tier-3 deferral (invariant-results recorded 'emergencyTransfer interaction with a live bank not driven (owner ejector seat, excluded by project precedent)' and deferred 'bank re-mints fresh supply post-sweep' to interaction analysis) — that deferral should be marked closed, not left open.
validityChecks.recommendation: RETAIN as L-02. Do not suppress. Keep the runbook framing exactly as written — if a future revision ever moves the recommendation INTO emergencyTransfer, it becomes a pe7m2 re-file and must be rejected at that point.

validityChecks.label: L-03

checks.inScope: PARTIAL — see nonStandardTokenAdjudication. This is a genuine hit and the only one in the run.
checks.evidence: PRECONDITION 1 of the finding's own attack path: 'the owner selects a hooked (ERC777-class) promo token.' ERC777 is the archetypal weird ERC-20 on every weird-erc20 list, and C4 rules it invalid by default. Without a hooked token there is no callback, no reentrancy window, and no finding at all — the non-standard token is not incidental colour, it is load-bearing on the trigger.

checks.note: Not this finding's mechanism — but the FoT PRECEDENT is what rescues it from outright INVALID. Verified in source at src/PhlimboV3.sol:401: `require(IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore == amount, "Fee-on-transfer not supported");` in startPromotion. Two consequences: (1) any future FoT finding against phlimbo-ea is INVALID — the protocol guards it explicitly, confirming run-07's decision to DROP L-04 (FoT) as known-invalid was correct; (2) the protocol demonstrably CURATES promo tokens for weirdness in this exact function, which is why a hook-curation gap in the same function is a coherent policy note rather than pure token-blaming.

checks.inScope: PARTIAL — the C4 rule 'unused view functions are QA at best' applies with unusual directness here, since the finding's entire impact runs THROUGH views (pendingPhUSD :993, pendingStable :1014, pendingPromo :1040) that no in-scope contract consumes. By the rule's own words this caps at QA.

checks.evidence: The harmed party does not exist. PRECONDITION 2 is 'a downstream integrator reads pendingPhUSD/pendingStable/pendingPromo as an entitlement oracle' and the finding concedes 'None identified in scope.' PhlimboV3's OWN accounting is correct throughout — the classifier states this plainly ('NO value at risk inside PhlimboV3 itself'; 'PhlimboV3's own accounting remains correct throughout'). So the demonstrated root cause (a real stale-debt window during _claimRewards, since realignment is caller-side at :715-717/:761-763/:808-810) produces NO demonstrated impact on anything that exists. The window is real; the victim is hypothetical.

checks.note: Not owner malice. But the footgun's non-obviousness is WEAKER than the classifier allows: ERC777 reentrancy hazards are among the most publicized in DeFi (imBTC/Uniswap, Lendf.me), so a competent operator selecting a promo token is closer to 'should know' than the classifier's 'has no reason to expect' concedes. This does not reach obvious-harm INVALID — the specific consequence (corrupting a third party's read of an UNRELATED accumulator, pendingPhUSD, via a PROMO token's callback) is genuinely non-obvious even to someone who knows ERC777 is dangerous. It does further weaken an already-floor-level Low.

nonStandardTokenAdjudication.whyNotOutrightInvalid: The C4 weird-token rule exists to stop contestants blaming a protocol for token weirdness the sponsor never intended to support — 'what if USDC rebased'. It fits poorly here for one specific reason: the promo token is an ARBITRARY, OWNER-SUPPLIED, ROTATING third-party token accepted at runtime by startPromotion (:391), backed by a whole promo rotation state machine. A surface DESIGNED to ingest arbitrary third-party tokens has token weirdness in scope by construction in a way a fixed USDC reward leg does not. The protocol itself concedes the point by curating for FoT at :401. So 'the curation list omits hooked tokens' is a legitimate observation about a first-party policy gap, not an unfalsifiable weird-token hypothetical.
nonStandardTokenAdjudication.whyNotFullyValidEither: Granting the ERC777 token entirely, the finding still lands nothing. Nothing in PhlimboV3 breaks; its accounting is correct at every point; the loss is suffered by an integrator that does not exist and may never. Two unestablished preconditions must coincide, and the classifier itself rates it 'implausible at present'. Under C4 the combination — weird-token trigger AND no demonstrated impact AND a hypothetical victim — would not survive as a Low security finding.
nonStandardTokenAdjudication.netVerdict: Survives as a QA-tier policy/documentation item. Does NOT survive as a Low security finding. The distinction matters because the Low label asserts a demonstrated impact this finding does not have.

validityChecks.notes: QUESTIONED — the only finding in the run to hit a known-invalid pattern squarely, and it hits three at partial strength (non-standard-token on the trigger, unused-view on the surface, speculation on the victim). It is NOT ruled INVALID: the read-only window is verified real in source, the reentrancy-checklist row is genuinely uncleared, and Law 1 forbids dropping an uncleared reentrancy row for tidiness — the classifier was right to surface it rather than swallow it. But its own boundaryNote already concedes the Low/QA line is arguable, and this stage's independent read is that the three pattern hits settle it on the QA side. Recorded here in full rather than acted on unilaterally: this is a recommendation to the human, not a suppression.
validityChecks.recommendation: RETAIN — do NOT drop (Law 1: an uncleared reentrancy row is a recall risk, and the window is real). RECOMMEND DOWNGRADE Low -> QA and REFRAME as a token-curation policy note: 'startPromotion curates promo tokens for fee-on-transfer (:401) but not for transfer hooks; mirror the FoT precedent by excluding hooked/ERC777 tokens in startPromotion's NatSpec, and document that the pending* views are not callback-safe.' That framing is defensible under every C4 rule this finding currently brushes against, costs nothing, and preserves the recall. Do NOT submit as a Low security finding in its current form — the weird-token trigger plus the nonexistent victim would not survive external review, and the pipeline rejects overstatement. ESCALATION: if any integrator is ever wired to the pending* views, re-weigh immediately — the victim becomes real and the calculus inverts.
validityChecks.doNotEscalateWithout: A named, existing consumer of the pending* views. Absent that, this must not climb above QA.

checks.note: Cross-repo (phlimbo-ea <-> phoenix-phase-2-staging) but both are registered first-party projects; the root cause (a foundry.toml pin) is in phlimbo-ea's own tree.

checks.evidence: The prospective leg is conditional on a wiring that DOES NOT EXIST. Verified by this agent with a FULL, UNTRUNCATED grep per the project's grep|head rule, since this is a negative claim: `grep -rIl 'PhlimboV3' lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/ | grep -v '/lib/'` returns ZERO first-party files. PhlimboV3 is not wired into phStaging in any form. The finding's own step 3 is explicitly conditional ('IF PhlimboV3 is wired into phStaging') and its residual risk is admittedly generic ('via_ir is a distinct Yul codegen pipeline with its own historical miscompilation record'). No defect is demonstrated — the finding says so itself: 'NOT AN ATTACK PATH', 'No defect demonstrated'.
checks.counterweight: The pattern does NOT bite cleanly, because what IS demonstrated is demonstrated empirically and in code that exists TODAY, not speculated: phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml:15 pins via_ir = false; phoenix-phase-2-staging/foundry.toml:7 sets via_ir = true — BOTH VERIFIED IN SOURCE BY THIS AGENT — and the two pipelines emit a measured 1,450 B / ~9% runtime bytecode delta. The root cause OF THE ASSURANCE GAP (a real, measured test/deploy codegen divergence against the established deploy vehicle that already ships Phlimbo V1/V2) is demonstrated. The root cause of any VULNERABILITY is not, and none is claimed.

adjudication.theDistinctionThatDecidesIt: 'Speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause' bars inventing a bug in code that does not exist. This finding does the opposite: it demonstrates a measured divergence between two files that both exist today, and then declines to invent a bug — explicitly. It is a demonstrated PROCESS gap about a PROSPECTIVE deploy, not a speculated VULNERABILITY. That is a real category and it is worth keeping; it is simply not a security finding, and the Low label implies one.
adjudication.usefulNegativeResultsAreTheRealValue: Two of this finding's outputs are more valuable than its severity and must survive any downgrade. (1) EIP-170 IS GENUINELY RESOLVED and is INDEPENDENT of via_ir — the via_ir build fits more comfortably (14,529 B, +10,047 B margin) than the legacy build (15,979 B, +8,597 B). So via_ir = false is NOT load-bearing for the size limit and can be revisited freely without reopening it. This is a hard, checkable fact that makes the preferred fix cheap, and it directly rebuts the reasoning in phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml's own comment block ('fits EIP-170 (~16 KB, +8.6 KB margin). Deploying with via_ir is safe...') by showing the via_ir build fits BETTER. (2) The CI-divergence sub-hypothesis was REFUTED, not left dangling (FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci inherits [profile.default], so via_ir=false there too; the real divergence is with phStaging). Recording a refutation so it is not re-investigated is exactly the discipline this pipeline wants.
adjudication.whatWouldMakeItInvalid: If it claimed or implied a via_ir miscompilation bug in PhlimboV3, it would be INVALID on the spot — pure speculation. It does not, and it is scrupulous about not doing so: the classifier explicitly declined to tag it faithfulness:true, noting the implementation does exactly what story-031 says and 'inventing [a defect] would be exactly the speculation the project rules forbid.' That restraint is why this is QUESTIONED and not INVALID.

validityChecks.notes: QUESTIONED on the label, not the substance. The finding is honest, empirically grounded, and useful — its own severityRationale concedes 'LOW / QA' in the same breath. But 'Low' asserts a demonstrated security impact and there is none; the finding's value is as a DEPLOY GATE and an assurance note. Under C4 a bare 'you should also test with via_ir' is a QA item, and this is that plus a measured delta.
validityChecks.recommendation: RETAIN — do not drop. RECOMMEND Low -> QA, reframed as a GATE on the V3 deploy story rather than a finding against the code: 'PhlimboV3 has zero test coverage of the bytecode the established deploy vehicle would produce (phStaging via_ir=true vs phlimbo-ea via_ir=false; measured 1,450 B delta). Close before the V3 deploy story lands — via_ir=false is not load-bearing for EIP-170, so re-enabling it is cheap.' The Low->QA move is largely cosmetic in this project's flow (qa-bundler bundles Low + QA together), which is precisely why the honest label costs nothing and should be taken. CROSS-PROJECT: the next phoenix-phase-2-staging run that wires PhlimboV3 must treat this as a blocking gate, not a note — carry it as a watch-note on that project.
validityChecks.carriedCaveat: The ENTIRE Tier-3 campaign (500k Foundry + 1.51M Medusa) inherits this gap and says nothing about the deployed bytecode — invariant-results.buildProvenance caveats this independently. That does not weaken those results for this run, but it must not be forgotten when the deploy story lands.

summary.headlineVerdict: M-01 IS VALID. It survives the reckless-admin challenge (the owner's action causes zero harm and passes its own smoke test; the freeze arms later via a third-party event with NO owner action at that moment — the C4 'external requirements' shape, not the 'admin does something visibly dumb' shape), the speculation challenge (the hook is shipped story-020 code with an interface, setter, event, ten tests, three live call sites and a PoC passing 8/8 — what is missing is a deployed instance, i.e. CONFIG, not CODE), and a third challenge this stage raised unprompted and answered on git provenance (intentional design). Submit as written; the write-up is honest and concedes its own strongest counter-argument in a dedicated section.
summary.newEvidenceThisStage: The intentional-design challenge — the project's own test_hook_revert_propagates_on_{stake,withdraw,claim} appearing to affirm the behaviour — was not in the brief and is the sharpest argument against M-01 available. It is refuted on the commit graph: IPhlimboHook.sol untouched since ac42de6 (story-020, a V2 commit); the withdraw test introduced by 8099db7 as a VERBATIM V2 PORT; story-030 (e32588d) deleted pauseWithdraw while touching NO hook file. Every artifact evidencing intent predates the change that made the consequence severe, and what was intended is atomicity ('state preserved on revert'), not a freeze with no exit. This strengthens M-01 beyond the classifier's own case, which argued the docblock is V2-scoped by its TEXT; it is now V2-scoped by its PROVENANCE.
concerns: L-03 is the only finding to hit a known-invalid pattern squarely, and it hits three at partial strength: non-standard-token (ERC777 trigger is load-bearing — no hooked token, no finding), unused-view (impact runs entirely through views no in-scope contract reads), and speculation (the harmed integrator does not exist; PhlimboV3's own accounting is correct throughout). Not INVALID — the read-only window is verified real, promo tokens are an arbitrary-token surface the protocol already curates for FoT at :401, and Law 1 forbids dropping an uncleared reentrancy row. But it should not carry a Low label that asserts an impact it does not have.

L-04 rides the speculation boundary: the phStaging wiring it depends on does not exist (verified: zero first-party PhlimboV3 references). It survives because the divergence is MEASURED in files that exist today and it explicitly declines to invent a defect — but it is an assurance/deploy gate, not a security finding.
Neither concern is grounds for suppression. Both are label/framing corrections routed to the human with reasoning recorded here.
